Whatcom County: 3,530 people in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025
HUD counted 1,912 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Whatcom County in 2025.
In Whatcom County, 3,530 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 182 from 3,712 in 2024. Those people lived in 1,912 households.
HUD reported 1,960 Housing Choice Vouchers available in the county, and 93% of those vouchers were in use.
HUD said 23% of those households were headed by a person it classifies as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $460 a month toward rent and utilities, up $4 from $456 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $17,345, up $402 from $16,943 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families receiving Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. That average covers families who obtained assistance, not applicants still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
